title: 1959 AHSME Problem 28
statement: In triangle \(ABC,\) \(\overline{AL}\) bisects angle \(A\) and \(\overline{CM}\) bisects angle \(C.\) Points \(L\) and \(M\) are on \(\overline{BC}\) and \(\overline{AB},\) respectively. The sides of triangle \(ABC\) are \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c.\) Then \(\dfrac{AM}{MB}=k\dfrac{CL}{LB},\) where \(k\) is:

solutions.text:
By the angle bisector theorem, \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{AM}{MB}&=\frac{AC}{CB}=\frac ba,\\ \frac{CL}{LB}&=\frac{AC}{AB}=\frac bc. \end{aligned} \] Therefore \[ k=\frac{\frac{b}{a}}{\frac{b}{c}}=\frac ca. \]

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Apply the angle bisector theorem separately to \(CM\) and \(AL\)
Use the standard notation \(a=BC,\ b=CA,\ c=AB\)
